newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money rises to 14.00/14.25 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money rises to 14.00/14.25 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money rose to 14.00/14.25 percent from 10.0/11.0 percent on Thursday morning on the back of relatively tight liquidity, dealers said.
They attributed it to higher withdrawals due to the lunar new year and Eid al-Fitr celebrations this weekend.
But some said the higher interbank rates were also partly driven up by rises in the swap market following short-covering by offshore operators ahead of the long weekend.
Overnight rupiah over tommorrow was traded at 16.0 percent.
Overnight swap was last at 1.0/1.1, up from an opening of 0.55/0.60 and tom/next at 4.5/4.6, up from 3.35/3.75.
The central bank supplied 417 billion rupiah on Thursday.
One local bank dealer said he was a bit worried about liquidity on Friday as it is the last day for liquidity reports and also the day before the local holidays for the festivals.
The central bank kept its rates for bilateral SBIs stable on Thursday. It offered six-day SBIs at nine percent, two-week at 10.0 percent, one- and three-month at 11.25 and 12.00 percent.
Longer-term were higher, with one- and three-month money quoted at 14.00 and 14.25 percent, respectively.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 10.86 percent, compared with 14.31 percent on Tuesday.
Bond dealers said prices remained stable and some trades were seen in PLN V/A and Astra bonds.
One bond dealer said the market was quiet as many players were already on holidays.
The yield of the benchmark PLN V/A bond was steady at 15.37 percent at the price of 105.25 percent.
